agent.assessment: Complete discrete dinuclear Pb(II) complex refined in P 1 21/c 1 with formula C45H31N5O9Pb2, consistent with three benzoates, two phenanthroline ligands, and nitrate. The original masked nine-site result was severely incomplete; reinterpretation and bonded Fourier completion recovered all 61 non-H atoms. Final anisotropic refinement with riding H atoms and no solvent mask gave R1(strong)=0.0422, wR2=0.1257, GooF=0.989. Metal coordination and molecular (0D) connectivity validate; this is not an extended MOF. P21/c is the unique top-ranked absence candidate and the complete model refines cleanly there.

Solved in centrosymmetric P 1 2/c 1. A controlled trial in tied alternative P 1 c 1 was unstable and decisively worse (R1 ~0.285 with 74 sites and ±14 e/A^3 residuals), whereas P 1 2/c 1 completed to a chemically coherent 2D Cd–O/N framework. Two diffuse carbon ghosts were deleted; C14X was reassigned O and C23X/C5/C13X were reassigned N, giving the exact expected non-H composition. Final anisotropic riding-H refinement: R1(strong)=0.0399, R1(all)=0.0454, wR2=0.1370, GooF=0.960, residual density +1.69/-1.30 e/A^3, with no ADP suspects. Cd1 is six-coordinate and Cd2 five-coordinate with plausible Cd–O/N distances. Final validation has no alerts and confidence 100.

agent.assessment: Solved in centrosymmetric C 1 2/n 1 (No. 15, nonstandard setting), which is supported by systematic absences, centric intensity statistics, and a substantially better trial than C 1 n 1. A fresh 0.8 A charge-flipping solution corrected the pipeline's severe element misassignment. The final model contains the expected Pt/Mo/K/O composition and is chemically consistent with an inorganic Pt-Mo polyoxometalate hydrate/alkali salt rather than a conventional organic MOF. Final anisotropic weighted refinement: R1(strong)=0.0595, wR2=0.1849, GooF=0.984. Both K sites have plausible O coordination; the second special-position K site restores the exact composition and improves R1.

C 1 2 1 is the best supported tested space group: the tied Cm alternative refined much worse (R1 strong 0.4289), while C2/m failed to produce a charge-flipping solution despite multiple seeds. The final retained C2 trajectory gives R1(strong)=0.2743, R1(all)=0.3712, wR2=0.5802 and GooF=3.389 with a solvent mask, after deleting isolated C9 and C122; residual extrema are +1.65/-1.55 e/A^3. However, this is not a chemically solved MOF. The apparent 3D framework is generated by gross overbuilding and impossible contacts (including Na-C distances down to about 1.15 A and Na-Na distances near 1.45-1.61 A). The model has far too many Na/C atoms and no assigned P or N relative to the composition hint, plus numerous very large or non-positive-definite ADPs. A restrained fresh C2 rebuild recovered the correct initial count of eight Na sites and several probable P sites but stalled near R1 0.42; it was therefore inferior as a density fit and did not yield a complete framework. The current result should be regarded only as partial electron-density phasing in likely C2, not as a valid refined chemical structure.
